??? quote "Dialogue"

    - You heard me sing it, the whole of it, all the way through. At last. Morven would have argued with every note.
    - Ailsa read it. An old song from a seat by the fire, and the Keeper of the Tide Book read it. I have not stopped weeping since.
    - Calder sang us her ending. Morven's ending. Oh, *Player*. I must sit down. I am sitting down. I must sit down more.
    - "He'll hear it when it's finished." Is that a promise or a punishment? I have decided it is a promise.
    - Ask, ask! An old man lives for questions. And free cups.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* The verse about the gap?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about Morven.
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Cormac, singer of the old songs of the shared camp, from when the Savage hunters and the Magicians first fished this inlet together. I tried sailmaking. I tried crewing. I sang through both and was thrown off both.
    - This seat by the fire has been mine since Malcolm kept the inn. Bethoc lets me flatter her for a cup. She is the finest landlady on Veligor, her ale is honest, and I mean every word.
    - Ah. You've heard me start it. "The hour the water forgets." An old pilot on the quay taught it me when I was a boy, made me say it till I had it perfect, and told me to keep it.
    - He was frightened, *Player*. I have never forgotten his face. And I've never been sure I have the end of it right. Morven had another version, I'd swear to it. Her grandson hums her tunes. He only smiles at me.
    - Morven's ending and mine, side by side at last. What it means is for wiser heads than mine. I only keep the songs.
    - Morven of the coves. The finest voice I ever heard. We sang together forty years and argued for thirty-nine of them about whose version was right.
    - When she died I sang for her at the shore and could not finish. Twenty years, and I never have. There. I've told you, and now I'm weeping. Don't mind me. I always do.
    - Go well, my friend, and come back to hear me weep.
